title: Research: sharp Eisenstein floor for adaptive affine public broadcasts
head: 42e80fe2c5baac8d0e259cfbe7b5479e5ab8d9ae
body:
PR 2017 proves a sharp 40b pairing-cost floor for fixed-support block-linear encoders on the forty Eisenstein lines. This contribution extends that floor to every execution of a finite adaptive affine public-broadcast tree, including variable query widths, supports, stopping times and nonlinear leaf decoders. The exact optimum is the total demand N=sum b_t, attained by direct singleton broadcasts; for equal demands this is 40b pointwise and under every input distribution.

The new interface argument proves that a reachable transcript's entire input fiber equals its frozen affine equation set. Kernel annihilation then extracts a fitting linear recovery matrix on that path, to which the retained good-reduction Schur-rank bound applies. The affine-fiber and row-space facts are standard; their source-bound adaptive application is the contribution. Every branch/header choice must be determined by previous paid answers, and every answer bit is charged. Private input-dependent metadata, localized observations and nonlinear node queries are excluded.

An actual globally nonlinear encoder (second answer z1+z0*z2) has affine queries and all paths cost 40. A variable-length version has path costs 40/44; block and unequal-demand fixtures use actual rational support prices. Under the additional inherited Eisenstein Dfc stage identity, the conditional replacement screen is D/T=(s-1)80b-2sC<=-80b. This is an abstract observation-model obstruction, not a native supplier, improved kappa or floor for arbitrary nonlinear codes.

Registered CPython 3.12.14 verification passed:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/eisenstein-adaptive-affine-floor
```

The primary replay executes the unchanged original PR 2017 verifier, then checks 2137 reachable leaves, 62768 complete kernel directions, exact whole-input accounting and seven effective controls. A separate literal-tree checker traverses 8320 inputs, checks 98816 receiver conflicts, 24 exact fibers and six rational support prices without importing new producer code. Git-free optimized replay, read-only defaults and eight source/receipt/tree/CLI corruption controls pass. A separate Codex agent reviewed proof/model/checkers and independently replayed both scientific commands on CPython 3.12.7; parent proof review also passed after correcting the singleton-price justification to use actual rational pairing rank.

Package: research/eisenstein-adaptive-affine-floor. Six retained sources are SHA-256/Git-blob pinned at freshly fetched canonical main 0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2, priority 4. Picker seed dea0cac7d7721c90e0a3629c8b5b4dbc selected complex-rank-shape-decoder; its ceiling and lever baselines passed before narrowing to this changed adaptive-interface obstruction. Complete final metadata overlap covers 798 open PRs at 15:55:59 UTC and 1252 Discussion records at 15:59:22 UTC on 2026-10-15. Main remained unchanged at 16:00 UTC. Coverage is not every diff or a novelty guarantee.

No physical realization, hosting, precision, compiler, full selected cold replay, independent human review or proof-assistant verification is claimed. Open next questions address fully priced localized observations and genuinely nonlinear payload queries.

Credit Jose Manuel's PR 2017 good-reduction bound, Jonathan Lam's PR 798 geometry/frame construction following Joel Pulikkan, Michael Fischler's PR 814 nonlinear boundary, Jerry Chen's Hurwitz adaptive-routing interface, and the retained project lineage. New work by ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proof, implementation, verification, documentation and separate-agent review. Apache-2.0; submitted for independent review.
